title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (TIPS 10-30Y, $500M cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35) — the row reads verbatim announce 9/14/2026, operation 9/15/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/16/2026, Liquidity Support, TIPS 10Y to 30Y, maturity range 09/16/2036 - 09/15/2056, min $0, max $500 million. Stays estimate on the same two counts as its nominal siblings: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 09-14 operation announcement rather than this document, checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 D-1 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08). This is the FIRST TIPS buyback operation this calendar has tracked, and it is filed for one specific analytical reason: it is the only OTHER long-end (10Y-30Y maturity) liquidity-support operation inside the 09-09 -> 11-04 doubled-size window, and sb0607 explicitly does NOT cover it — the release names 'the 10-year to 20-year sector and the 20-year to 30-year sector' of NOMINAL coupons only. So it is the untouched control against which the doubled nominal ops are read. The contrast is stark and primary-verified (fiscaldata buybacks_operations, fetched 2026-09-08): the nominal long end fills its cap essentially always (10Y-20Y 25/25, 20Y-30Y 24/26 since 2024-05) while the TIPS 10Y-30Y bucket has never come close — 2025-11-12 offered $1.392B / accepted $142M, 2025-12-23 $1.190B / $108M, 2026-03-25 $757M / $110M, 2026-05-28 $784M / $91M, i.e. roughly a 10-28% fill of a $500M cap across 4 of the 4 operations in that window. THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT: in nominals the cap was the binding constraint, in TIPS it never was, which is exactly why Treasury raised one and not the other. Low impact is honest about size — $500M against a $61B 10Y+30Y issuance week is noise — not about analytical value. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
